page: Microsoft Azure L32ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on 64-bit ARM architecture and provisioned via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation.

Storage architecture is a primary highlight of this configuration, incorporating 7680 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage alongside support for Premium Storage volumes. This direct-attached NVMe disk array provides low latency and high bandwidth for applications with heavy local input and output demands. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, focusing entirely on general compute and storage throughput.

The use of ARM processor technology introduces high compute density and resource efficiency for native ARM applications. However, organizations must consider software compatibility, as x86 instruction sets and specific hardware vector extensions are absent. Additionally, the instance configuration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network ingress planning.

Given its combination of high storage capacity, substantial memory allocation, and dedicated multi-core compute, the L32ps_v5 serves demanding storage and data-tier workloads. Typical operational fits include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional database management systems, big data processing pipelines, and search indexing engines.
description: Microsoft Azure L32ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by 64-bit ARM architecture on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of memory, establishing an 8 GB per core ratio suited for memory-intensive operations. A core characteristic of the instance is its local storage configuration, which includes 7680 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity to address intensive input and output demands. The system lacks discrete GPU accelerators and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The ARM-based processor implementation provides an efficient resource footprint for scalable environments, though workloads must be natively compatible with the arm64 architecture. Given its substantial local disk capacity and dedicated compute allocation, the L32ps_v5 is designed for data-intensive workloads such as distributed databases, log indexing clusters, transactional databases, and real-time analytical platforms requiring high local storage throughput.
